These fixtures were recorded on 2026-11-07 with Claude Code 2.1.319 and Codex 0.167.0, each in an isolated home with UserPromptSubmit and Stop hooks that saved their input. Session, prompt, turn, task and message identifiers and filesystem paths were replaced with test values; prompts and assistant text are as recorded.

- Both hooks of one turn carry the same turn id: Claude Code's `prompt_id`, Codex's `turn_id`.
- A Claude Code Stop with a background shell still running lists it in `background_tasks` with status `running`. The completion arrives later as a new prompt with its own `prompt_id`, and no field of that prompt tells it apart from one the person typed.
- An interrupted turn gets no Stop on either host. Claude Code writes a `[Request interrupted by user]` user record for that prompt; Codex writes an `event_msg` of type `turn_aborted` for that turn.
- When another Stop hook blocks, Claude Code fires a second Stop for the same `prompt_id`. Every Stop hook gets the first Stop at once, with `stop_hook_active` false and the text the model has just written, so none of them can see the block. Claude Code then appends a meta user record, "Stop hook feedback:" plus the block reason, and a `system` record of subtype `stop_hook_summary` listing the reason in `hookErrors`. It continues the turn, and the second Stop has `stop_hook_active` true and the turn's real final text. Each Stop gets a summary once all its hooks have exited. `claude-2.1.319-blocked-stop.jsonl` holds the records Claude Code wrote after the first Stop's text: the feedback, then the two summaries. It was recorded with `claude -p` and a second Stop hook that blocked once.
- `claude-2.1.319-background-turns.jsonl` is one session's transcript, recorded on 2026-11-09 with the same Stop and prompt hooks, with API request records, file snapshots and other attachments' bodies left out. In `prompt-start` a background Bash records `backgroundTaskId` in its tool result. `task-first` ends while `prompt-busy` runs, so Claude Code queues its notice into that turn as a `queued_command` attachment, which carries no `promptId`, and also runs the prompt hook with the notice as the prompt and `prompt-busy`'s `prompt_id`. `task-second` ends while the session is idle, so its notice is `prompt-notice`'s own prompt, a user record whose `origin.kind` is `task-notification`. `queue-operation` records log every notice, including ones that become their own prompt.
